bug_semantics: Bandit's HTTP/1 chunked-body reader silently ignores the caller-supplied Plug.Conn :length cap (Plug.Parsers default 8_000_000) and buffers the entire Transfer-Encoding: chunked request into memory before the application runs. At the advisory snapshot this is Bandit.HTTP1.Socket.read_data/2 (chunked clause) calling do_read_chunked_data!/5 in lib/bandit/http1/socket.ex: it forwards only :read_length and :read_timeout, recursively concatenates every chunk into an iolist, materializes it with IO.iodata_to_binary/1, and always returns {:ok, body, ...} never {:more, ...}, so callers cannot emit 413. The content-length sibling in the same module correctly does min(unread, Keyword.get(opts, :length, 8_000_000)). Because Plug.Parsers runs before routing and auth on a typical Phoenix endpoint, any unauthenticated chunked POST with a matching Content-Type can OOM the BEAM. Hex/CNA range is bandit >= 1.4.0 < 1.11.1; GHSA-9q9q-324x-93r2 withdrawn_at is null; EEF CNA CVE-2026-39803 is published (not rejected).
flaw_origin: The unbounded chunked reader was first written on 2019-11-19 in 57b9722b589ca9177a5b88bedc999dee6338cfe6 (Flesh out chunked encoding reads) as do_read_chunk/3 in lib/bandit/http1_request.ex. That commit replaced a non-working WIP stub with a recursive loop that does body <> next_chunk and returns {:ok, body, req} on the terminating 0-size chunk. opts is passed only into grow_buffer(..., :all_available, opts), which uses :read_length/:read_timeout and never :length, while the content-length clause in the same file already capped with Keyword.get(opts, :length, 8_000_000). Later commits 08e06d3e, 68e44aec, and 903e209a only renamed/moved that already-unbounded loop (adapter do_read_chunk -> do_read_chunked_body -> socket do_read_chunked_data!); 903e209a is the CNA git Introduced event only because it created socket.ex, not because it first wrote the mechanism.
